bss.topic: O trabalho ontem e hoje: tecnologia e mudanças

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que é uma profissão?
options: Um trabalho que a pessoa faz para ganhar a vida
questions.answer: Um trabalho que a pessoa faz para ganhar a vida
questions.hint: Pense no que os adultos fazem durante o dia para receber dinheiro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Antigamente, muitas roupas eram lavadas:
options: à mão, no tanque ou no rio
questions.answer: à mão, no tanque ou no rio
questions.hint: Pense em como era a vida antes de existir eletricidade em todas as casas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destas máquinas ajudou a mudar o trabalho no campo?
questions.hint: Qual máquina ajuda a arar a terra?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Antes do telefone celular, que aparelho fixo em casa as pessoas usavam para conversar a distância?
questions.hint: Ele ficava preso a um fio na parede.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Uma profissão que quase desapareceu com a chegada do telefone automático foi:
questions.hint: Pense em quem completava as ligações à mão antigamente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual profissão surgiu por causa da internet?
questions.hint: Qual delas precisa de um computador conectado?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O acendedor de lampiões acendia as luzes da rua. Por que essa profissão acabou?
options: Porque as pessoas pararam de sair
questions.hint: Pense no que hoje acende as luzes da rua sozinho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: No passado, as cartas eram a forma mais comum de mandar notícias para longe. Hoje usamos muito:
questions.hint: Pense no que sua família usa para falar com parentes distantes.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chama a pessoa que entrega as cartas nas casas?
questions.hint: A palavra vem de 'carta'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual frase mostra uma vantagem da tecnologia no trabalho?
options: Algumas tarefas pesadas ficam mais fáceis e rápidas
As pessoas nunca mais se cansam
questions.answer: Algumas tarefas pesadas ficam mais fáceis e rápidas
questions.hint: Pense em uma máquina que poupa esforço.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual frase mostra um desafio causado pela tecnologia?
options: Algumas pessoas precisam aprender novas habilidades para não perder o emprego
O trabalho fica sempre mais lento
questions.answer: Algumas pessoas precisam aprender novas habilidades para não perder o emprego
questions.hint: O que acontece com quem fazia um trabalho que agora uma máquina faz?

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Na agricultura de antigamente, a colheita era feita principalmente:
options: com as mãos e ferramentas simples
questions.answer: com as mãos e ferramentas simples
questions.hint: Pense em enxadas e cestos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que profissão continua existindo há muito tempo e cuida da saúde das pessoas?
questions.hint: Você vai a essa pessoa quando fica doente.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que quer dizer 'comparar' o trabalho de ontem e de hoje?
options: Ver o que é parecido e o que é diferente
questions.answer: Ver o que é parecido e o que é diferente
questions.hint: Comparar é olhar duas coisas lado a lado.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Escolha uma profissão (por exemplo, professor ou padeiro). Diga uma coisa que mudou nela com a tecnologia e uma que continua igual.
questions.hint: Pense nas ferramentas que essa pessoa usava antes e usa agora.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Você acha que no futuro vão surgir profissões novas? Dê um exemplo e explique por quê.
questions.hint: Pense nas tecnologias que estão aparecendo hoje.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does it mean to proof-read your writing?
options: Write it again from the start
Read it to a friend quickly
questions.hint: Think about what an editor looks for.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Correct the spelling: becaus
questions.hint: Say it slowly: be-cause.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Correct the spelling: freind
questions.hint: Look closely at the order of the vowels in the middle.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is the correct choice? 'We ___ going to the park.'
questions.hint: 'We' is plural, and this is about the past.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses an apostrophe correctly?
questions.hint: The apostrophe shows that something belongs to one dog.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Cohesion means that a piece of writing:
questions.hint: Think about how ideas join from one sentence to the next.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word is a good adverbial to start a new paragraph about later events?
questions.hint: You need a word that tells the reader when.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Choose the best pronoun to avoid repeating the name: 'Leo opened the box. ___ found a key inside.'
questions.hint: We already know who Leo is.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which conjunction best joins these ideas? 'It was raining, ___ we stayed inside.'
questions.hint: The second part is the result of the first.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word could replace 'nice' to make this sentence more precise? 'We had a nice day at the zoo.'
questions.hint: Pick a stronger adjective.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence has inverted commas (speech marks) in the right place?
questions.hint: Only the words that are spoken go inside.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: In a piece of writing, why do we start a new paragraph?
options: To show a new time, place, idea or speaker
questions.answer: To show a new time, place, idea or speaker
questions.hint: Think about what changes in the story.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Improve this sentence by adding a fronted adverbial and a more interesting verb: 'The cat went up the tree.'
questions.hint: Start with a phrase that tells when, where or how, followed by a comma.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: familly → family; bilt → built; desided → decided; beter → better; brillant → brilliant
questions.hint: Look for missing or wrong letters.
questions.text: Last Saturday, my familly went to the beach. We bilt a huge sandcastle with towers and a moat. Then the tide came in and washed it away. My little brother was very upset, so we desided to build another one. It was even beter than the first. We had a brillant day.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: suprised → surprised; beacause → because; definitly → definitely; agian → again
questions.hint: Read one word at a time, as if you were the teacher marking it.
questions.text: On our school trip, we visited a farm. The farmer showed us how to feed the sheep and collect eggs. I was suprised how warm the eggs felt. Later, we had our lunch under a tree beacause it was so sunny. I would definitly like to go agian.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
questions.hint: Check the capital letter, the comma and the end mark.

en_read.topic: Fact, opinion and bias in news reports

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a fact?
options: Something that can be proved true
questions.answer: Something that can be proved true
questions.hint: Could you check it in an encyclopedia?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is an opinion?
questions.hint: Different people might disagree about it.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is a fact?
options: The new library opened on Monday.
The new library is the best place in town.
Everyone will love the new library.
questions.answer: The new library opened on Monday.
questions.hint: Which one could you check is true?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which sentence is an opinion?
options: Football is the most exciting sport.
A football team has eleven players on the pitch.
The match started at three o'clock.
questions.answer: Football is the most exciting sport.
questions.hint: Look for a word that shows someone's feeling.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Fact or opinion? 'Water freezes at 0 °C.'
questions.hint: Could a scientist test it?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Fact or opinion? 'Spinach tastes horrible.'
questions.hint: Would everybody agree?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which word often signals an opinion?
questions.hint: Which word describes a feeling about something?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What is a headline?
options: The title at the top of a news report
The last sentence of a report
questions.answer: The title at the top of a news report
questions.hint: It's the first thing you read, in big letters.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why do headlines often use short, dramatic words?
questions.hint: Think about why you might choose to read one story over another.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: What does 'bias' mean in a news report?
options: Showing only one side of a story
questions.answer: Showing only one side of a story
questions.hint: Is the report fair to everyone?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which headline is the most biased?
options: Park to Close for Two Weeks
questions.hint: Look for words that judge people.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Which headline is the most neutral?
questions.hint: Which one just tells you what happened?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: A report says: 'Local hero Sam saved the day.' Which word shows the writer's opinion?
questions.hint: Which word praises the person?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: If a report only includes interviews with people who agree with one side, it is:
questions.hint: Are all views being heard?

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Rewrite this headline so it is neutral: 'Greedy Shop Owners Steal Our Money With Silly Prices'.
questions.hint: Remove the words that show feelings and keep what happened.

questions.subject: en_read
questions.q: Why is it important for readers to notice bias in the news?
questions.hint: Think about how a one-sided story could change what you believe.
